description: Fires in late endgames (about 4-16 empty cells left) when column 1 is completely full AND the player to move is lost: the opponent wins by force within a few moves, whatever I play. It is strongest when most columns are full and only one or two columns are left. If column 1 has any empty cell it stays silent, even in lost positions. Won or drawn endgames with column 1 full mostly stay below threshold.
effect: Forced high, it removes column 1 from the policy (e.g. 0.32 -> 0.00 when column 1 was still legal) and flattens the distribution, cutting the favourite (often centre column 3) by about 30 points and spreading that probability to the other columns. Zeroing it in firing positions changes move probabilities by <= 0.05, since those are near-forced endgames.
notes: Column-1-full is a hard gate: in 2,900 sampled examples, none fire with column 1 open, and in a minimal pair (dev 16914 game) lost positions with column 1 open read -1.4 while filling column 1 gives 17.2. Within column-1-full endgames, activation tracks the sign of the engine score ply by ply (lost -> high). The program uses an exact small endgame solver. Dev: col1-full + empty-count only F1 0.38; + solver-lost 0.60; + loss within 7 plies 0.64; final 0.649 (P 0.56, R 0.78, AUROC 0.88), sim share 0.47. Doubts: about 40% of lost col1-full endgames sit just under threshold, and some won/drawn ones fire, so the unit is graded and follows the model's own judgment, not the exact game value. Solver gives up above 16 empty cells, so early cases are missed. Synthesis: hill-climbed move-order swaps of dev games, 20.0-23.0 vs dev max 18.7.
